title: Direct-sum lower bound for independent modular Sum-Equal instances
author: Elbert Du, Michael Mitzenmacher, David Woodruff, and Guang Yang
work: Separating k-Player from t-Player One-Way Communication, with Applications to Data Streams
source_version: Theory of Computing19 (2023), Article10, publisher source publicationDecember 31, 2023; DOI10.4086/toc.2023.v019a010

source_locator.proof_scope: Complete author argument including supplied core constructions

difficulty_reason: The new obligation is a multiplicative k-party direct sum with per-instance reconstruction, where ordinary two-party information-complexity direct sums do not supply the claimed bound. The author core builds a large-rectangle entropy-to-min-entropy conversion and an induction that keeps linearly many coordinates jointly near-uniform after conditioning on previous copies. It then relates the vector Hamming-error mass to rectangle probabilities and obtains the communication contradiction, retaining the complete deferred lemma and claim proofs.

source_check.note: Full original definitions and article context retained. Selected Theorem6.1 requires prime p in(k^(1/4),2k^(1/4)), m=o(k^(1/4)), delta in(0,1/9), and success for every fixed coordinate with a reconstruction function; do not promote unrestricted m or simultaneous all-coordinate correctness. Author flips only the vector output F at1113; that explicit convention is retained. Primary proof1112–1250, complete Hamming-ball claim1254–1298, complete partial-uniformity induction1302–1529. External rectangle decomposition is cited Viola Claim24/Kushilevitz–NisanLemma1.16; the finite-field mixing prerequisite is ViolaClaim31 in the exact stated corrected exponent, with author remark1494–1497. The distinct Theorem5.7 and strict-turnstile outcome have unresolved source-scope holds and are retained solely as unqualified original context, never counted for this unit. Supporting lemma/claim and corollaries uncounted.
